Fact.Name: Schedule C businesses
Fact.Description: One or more sole-proprietor / gig businesses reported on Schedule C. Gross income inclusion authority: 26 U.S.C. § 61.

Fact.Name: Schedule C businesses done
Fact.Description: Filer finished the Schedule C business loop.

Fact.Name: Has Schedule C businesses
Fact.Description: Whether any Schedule C businesses are listed.

Fact.Name: A Schedule C business still uses the single expense total
Fact.Description: True when any Schedule C business still uses the pre-line-item expense total (/scheduleCBusinesses/*/usesLegacyExpenseBucket). False when there is no Schedule C, and when every business is on the line-item path. A mixed return stays true: PA-40 line 4 is one sum, so a business that cannot be mapped onto PA Schedule C keeps /flowKnockoutPaScheduleC true. The count is not read when there is no Schedule C, so a W-2-only return stays complete.

Fact.Name: Had self-employment / gig / freelance income
Fact.Description: Interview gate: whether the filer (or spouse) had self-employment, gig, or freelance income that belongs on Schedule C. Gap evidence Pub 6048 excluded this from upstream Direct File: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p6048.pdf

Fact.Name: Wants qualified business income deduction (no longer asked)
Fact.Description: Kept so saved returns still load. The 26 U.S.C. 199A(a) deduction is not elective (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/199A), and Form 8995 (form8995.xml, #87) now computes it, so this answer is not used anywhere.

Fact.Name: Knockout: Schedule C QBI deduction case Form 8995 here can't compute
Fact.Description: #87: Schedule C qualified business income is computed on Form 8995 (form8995.xml). This is true when the return has Schedule C qualified business income and any Form 8995 stop applies: a prior-year loss carryforward, a cooperative patron, active and non-active trades together, or taxable income before the deduction above the threshold (Form 8995-A). A section 162 rental with no Schedule C does not make this true. Each part is its own BlockSubmissionOnTrue fact in /flowIsKnockedOut (#186). Used for the Schedule C knockout screen.

Fact.Name: Schedule C businesses owned by the secondary filer
Secondary filer's Schedule C net profit or (loss)
Fact.Description: #118. Sum of /scheduleCBusinesses/*/netProfitOrLoss for the businesses the secondary filer owns: the line 3 of that spouse's own Schedule SE. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule SE, PDF p. 3: "If both spouses have self-employment income, each must file a separate Schedule SE." $0 on a return that isn't a joint return (only a joint return reports a spouse's business) or when the filer answered no to self-employment income; incomplete while businesses are still being entered, like /scheduleCNetProfitOrLoss.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's Schedule C net profit or (loss)
Fact.Description: #118. Every business not owned by the secondary filer is the primary filer's (/scheduleCBusinesses/*/filer defaults to the primary filer), so this is /scheduleCNetProfitOrLoss minus /scheduleCSecondaryFilerNetProfitOrLoss, and the two always add up to Schedule 1 line 3.

Fact.Name: Knockout: spouse-owned Schedule C business
Fact.Description: Schedule SE is figured per filer (scheduleSE /secondaryFilerSelfEmploymentTax, with that spouse's own OASDI base under 26 U.S.C. 1402(b)(1)) and Schedule 2 line 4, Schedule 1 line 15 and Form 8959 line 13 combine both. A secondary filer's business still stops the return until the rest of that spouse's path is per spouse: EITC and CDCC earned income with self-employment (Form 2441 lines 4 and 5 are per spouse), and the printed return has no Schedule SE form yet (one per spouse once it does).

Fact.Name: Knockout: Schedule C cases the EITC, CDCC or ACTC earned income can't yet figure
Fact.Description: #117. The EITC (eitc /eitcEarnedIncomeWithoutCombatPay), the CDCC (income /primaryFilerEarnedIncomeForCdccBase) and the ACTC (income /earnedIncomeWithAllCombatPay) add /scheduleCNetProfitForEarnedIncome. Still stopped: - A Schedule C net loss. Both sources say a loss reduces earned income: Instructions for Form 1040 (2025), PDF p. 47, EIC Worksheet B, line 1e and line 4b ("Combine lines 1e, 2c, 3, and 4a"), and the 2026 draft Instructions for Form 2441, PDF p. 5 ("You must reduce your earned income by any loss from self-employment"). /scheduleCNetProfitForEarnedIncome is floored at $0, so a loss stops the return when the EITC could apply (AGI below the EITC completed phaseout, eitc /belowEitcAgiLimit, or eitc /eitcQualified), the CDCC applies or the CTC applies. A loss can lower earned income below the EITC limit even when wages alone are above it, so the EITC test is on AGI, which already includes the loss. - A joint return with any Schedule C result and the CDCC: Form 2441 lines 4 and 5 need each spouse's Schedule SE line 3 and Schedule 1 line 15 share ("If filing jointly, figure your and your spouse's earned income separately"), and Schedule SE is not yet figured per spouse. Stopped elsewhere: a spouse-owned business (/flowKnockoutScheduleCSpouseBusiness), statutory employees (formW2s /flowKnockoutStatutoryEmployee), and farm income, church employee income, the optional methods, ministry or Forms 4361 and 4029, notary fees, and Form 8919 wages (scheduleSE /flowKnockoutScheduleSEOutOfScope). Complete and false when there is no Schedule C or the Schedule C result is a profit on a return that isn't a joint return claiming the CDCC.

Fact.Name: Business owner (filer)
Fact.Description: Which filer owns this Schedule C business.

Fact.Name: Business name
Fact.Description: Schedule C identifying information — principal business / professional activity name.

Fact.Name: Gross receipts or sales
Fact.Description: Schedule C Part I gross receipts (cash MVP). Inclusion: 26 U.S.C. § 61. Cite Schedule C instructions PDF page for the line rule used in the implementation PR notes.

Fact.Name: Gross receipts or sales (derived)
Fact.Description: Gross receipts defaulting incomplete writable to zero for sums.

Fact.Name: Total business expenses (MVP)
Fact.Description: MVP expense bucket (sum of deductible trade/business expenses). Authority: 26 U.S.C. § 162 (ordinary and necessary expenses paid or incurred in carrying on a trade or business) — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/162 Kept for a return that already stored one total. The interview now asks the Schedule C lines. Once any line-item answer is complete, this total is ignored.

Fact.Name: Total business expenses (derived)
Fact.Description: Schedule C line 28. On a return that only stored one expense total, that total. On the line-item path, the sum of the supported lines, and only when no out-of-scope form applies. Otherwise incomplete: an unanswered expense is not treated as zero. 26 U.S.C. 162(a).

Fact.Name: Net profit or (loss)
Fact.Description: Schedule C line 31. Single-total path: gross receipts minus that total. Line-item path: line 7 minus line 28, and only when line 7 and line 28 are complete and no out-of-scope form applies. A loss that needs Form 6198 or Form 8582 is still computed and is stopped by /flowKnockoutScheduleCOutOfScope, because the stop reads this result and this result must not read the stop. 26 U.S.C. 61, 162, 465, 469.

Fact.Name: Schedule C business complete
Fact.Description: Single-total path: name, gross receipts, the expense total, and material participation. Line-item path: name, material participation, Part I amounts, and every stop question. A form stop completes the business without expense amounts. Otherwise the expense lines, line 7, and line 28 must be complete, and a loss needs the at-risk answer.

Fact.Name: Filer materially participates in this business
Fact.Description: 26 U.S.C. 199A(i)(2)(B): "The term 'active qualified trade or business' means ... any qualified trade or business of the taxpayer in which the taxpayer materially participates (within the meaning of section 469(h))." 26 U.S.C. 469(h)(1) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/469): material participation means involvement in the operations of the activity "on a basis which is (A) regular, (B) continuous, and (C) substantial." Used for Form 8995 line 16 (minimum deduction).

Fact.Name: Filer does not materially participate in this business
Schedule C businesses with material participation
Schedule C businesses without material participation
Schedule C expense line choices
Fact.Description: Part II lines this tool can deduct under 26 U.S.C. 162(a) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/162), plus Part V. Lines that need another form are separate yes/no stops, not choices.

Fact.Name: Returns and allowances
Fact.Description: Schedule C line 2. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 7, Line 2: report sales returns and allowances as a positive number. 26 U.S.C. 61.

Fact.Name: Other business income
Fact.Description: Schedule C line 6, ordinary other business income (scrap, recovered bad debts, interest on receivables). 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 7, Line 6. Fuel tax credits and Form 4797 recapture are a separate stop. 26 U.S.C. 61.

Fact.Name: Other business income is above zero
Fact.Description: True when line 6 is greater than zero, so the filer must say whether that income needs another form.

Fact.Name: Line 6 needs another form
Fact.Description: 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 7, Line 6: federal and state gasoline or fuel tax credit and recapture of a section 179 deduction or listed property (Form 4797) are included on line 6. This tool does not compute those. Yes stops the return.

Fact.Name: Gross receipts test amount for a small business taxpayer
Fact.Description: Rev. Proc. 2025-32 §4.30, PDF p. 23 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-32.pdf): "For taxable years beginning in 2026, a corporation or partnership meets the gross receipts test of § 448(c) for any taxable year if the average annual gross receipts of such entity for the 3-taxable-year period ending with the taxable year which precedes such taxable year does not exceed $32,000,000." 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 16: "You qualify as a small business taxpayer if you (a) have average annual gross receipts of $32 million or less for the 3 prior tax years (indexed for inflation), and (b) are not a tax shelter (as defined in section 448(d)(3))." 26 U.S.C. 448(c)(1) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/448) states the 3-taxable-year test. The $25,000,000 statutory amount is adjusted by the revenue procedure. 26 U.S.C. 471(c)(1) and 263A(i)(1) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/471, https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/263A) use that test, and only for a taxpayer who is not a tax shelter prohibited from using the cash method under section 448(a)(3). 26 U.S.C. 471(c)(3) and 263A(i)(2) apply the test to an individual as if each trade or business were a corporation or partnership. The filer enters the 3-prior-year average. This fact is the amount that average is compared with. An average equal to $32,000,000 still meets the test ("does not exceed"). This year's Schedule C line 1 is not the test.

Fact.Name: Schedule C closing-inventory methods
Fact.Description: 2026 Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1040sc.pdf, SHA-256 cc44e7d1150e54d991835814c1191f60a32617730ca9e50e6f532b51293a86b4), PDF p. 2, line 33: "Method(s) used to value closing inventory: a Cost, b Lower of cost or market, c Other (attach explanation)." 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 17, Line 33: "Your inventories can be valued at cost, the lower of cost or market, or any other method approved by the IRS." The fourth choice is the 26 U.S.C. 471(c)(1)(B)(i) method that does not keep an inventory (instructions, PDF p. 16).

Fact.Name: Inventory or cost of goods sold
Fact.Description: Schedule C line 4 and Part III. 26 U.S.C. 471(a) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/471): inventories are taken when necessary to clearly determine income. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 16, Cost of Goods Sold. No means this business does not complete Part III, and line 4 is zero. Yes asks for the line 33 method. Cost or lower of cost or market, with line 34 no, line 42 not below zero, line 35 equal to last year's closing inventory, a 3-prior-year average that does not exceed the Rev. Proc. 2025-32 §4.30 amount, and the filer not a tax shelter, is figured in Part III. Any other answer stops the return.

Fact.Name: Method used to value closing inventory
Fact.Description: Schedule C line 33, asked only when this business has inventory or cost of goods sold. Cost and lower of cost or market are the simple methods this tool figures. "Other" is line 33c and stops the return. Nonincidental materials and supplies is the 26 U.S.C. 471(c)(1)(B)(i) method of not keeping an inventory; claiming it while Part III is still required stops the return. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C, PDF p. 16 and PDF p. 17.

Fact.Name: Line 33a, cost
Fact.Description: Closing inventory is valued at cost. 2026 Schedule C, PDF p. 2, line 33a.

Fact.Name: Line 33b, lower of cost or market
Fact.Description: Closing inventory is valued at the lower of cost or market. 2026 Schedule C, PDF p. 2, line 33b.

Fact.Name: Line 33c, other
Fact.Description: Line 33c, "Other (attach explanation)." Not cost or lower of cost or market. Stops the return. 2026 Schedule C, PDF p. 2. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C, PDF p. 17, Line 33.

Fact.Name: No-inventory method under section 471(c)
Fact.Description: 26 U.S.C. 471(c)(1)(B)(i): the method "treats inventory as non-incidental materials and supplies." 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C, PDF p. 16: "If you choose not to keep an inventory" and account for it as nonincidental materials and supplies, Part III is not completed. Choosing that method while this business still needs Part III is inconsistent and stops the return.

Fact.Name: Closing inventory uses cost or lower of cost or market
Fact.Description: Line 33a or line 33b. These are the Part III methods this tool figures. Line 33c and the section 471(c) no-inventory method are not.

Fact.Name: Change in inventory quantities, costs, or valuations
Fact.Description: Schedule C line 34. 2026 Schedule C, PDF p. 2: "Was there any change in determining quantities, costs, or valuations between opening and closing inventory? If "Yes," attach explanation." Yes stops the return. This tool does not compute a change in method or a section 481(a) adjustment. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C, PDF p. 17, Line 35, describes refiguring last year's closing inventory when the method changes.

Fact.Name: Ask the small-business taxpayer questions
Fact.Description: True when Part III would otherwise be the simple path: inventory, line 33a or 33b, and line 34 no. The 3-prior-year average and the tax-shelter question are asked then. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C, PDF p. 16.

Fact.Name: Average annual gross receipts for the 3 prior tax years
Fact.Description: The section 448(c) average the filer has already figured: the 3-taxable-year period ending with the taxable year which precedes this year, including a predecessor and with a short year annualized. 26 U.S.C. 448(c)(1) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/448). 26 U.S.C. 448(c)(2) counts related persons treated as a single employer as one person. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 16: "If your business has not been in existence for all of the 3-tax-year period used in figuring average gross receipts, base your average on the period it has existed," and annualize a short year. Enter zero when the business did not exist in those years. This year's Schedule C line 1 is not this average. Compared with /scheduleCSmallBusinessGrossReceiptsLimit. Rev. Proc. 2025-32 §4.30, PDF p. 23: the test "does not exceed $32,000,000."

Fact.Name: 3-prior-year average exceeds the gross receipts test amount
Fact.Description: True when the entered average is greater than $32,000,000. Rev. Proc. 2025-32 §4.30, PDF p. 23: the section 448(c) test "does not exceed $32,000,000." Equal to $32,000,000 still meets the test. 26 U.S.C. 471(c)(1) and 263A(i)(1) do not apply when the test is not met, so simple Part III stops.

Fact.Name: Taxpayer is a tax shelter
Fact.Description: 26 U.S.C. 448(d)(3) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/448): "The term 'tax shelter' has the meaning given such term by section 461(i)(3) (determined after application of paragraph (4) thereof)." 26 U.S.C. 471(c)(1) and 263A(i)(1) do not apply to a tax shelter prohibited from using the cash method under section 448(a)(3). 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C, PDF p. 16: a small business taxpayer "(b) are not a tax shelter (as defined in section 448(d)(3))." Yes stops simple Part III.

Fact.Name: Line 35 differs from last year's closing inventory
Fact.Description: Screener for Schedule C line 35. 2026 Schedule C, PDF p. 2: "Inventory at beginning of year. If different from last year's closing inventory, attach explanation." 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C, PDF p. 17, Line 35: "If there is a difference between last year's closing inventory and the refigured amount, attach an explanation." This tool does not attach that explanation. Yes stops the return. No means line 35 matches last year's closing inventory and Part III can continue.

Fact.Name: Inventory at beginning of year
Fact.Description: Schedule C line 35. 2026 Schedule C, PDF p. 2: "Inventory at beginning of year. If different from last year's closing inventory, attach explanation."

Fact.Name: Purchases
Fact.Description: Purchases included in Schedule C line 36 before subtracting items withdrawn for personal use. 2026 Schedule C, PDF p. 2, line 36: "Purchases less cost of items withdrawn for personal use."

Fact.Name: Cost of items withdrawn for personal use
Fact.Description: Subtracted from purchases to reach Schedule C line 36. 2026 Schedule C, PDF p. 2, line 36: "Purchases less cost of items withdrawn for personal use." Enter zero when nothing was withdrawn.

Fact.Name: Cost of labor
Fact.Description: Schedule C line 37. 2026 Schedule C, PDF p. 2: "Cost of labor. Do not include any amounts paid to yourself."

Fact.Name: Materials and supplies
Fact.Description: Schedule C line 38. 2026 Schedule C, PDF p. 2: "Materials and supplies."

Fact.Name: Other costs
Fact.Description: Schedule C line 39. 2026 Schedule C, PDF p. 2: "Other costs." Uniform capitalization under 26 U.S.C. 263A (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/263A) is not computed. 26 U.S.C. 263A(i)(1) turns section 263A off only for a taxpayer that meets the section 448(c) test and is not a tax shelter. A business that fails that test, or is a tax shelter, stops before these costs are used.

Fact.Name: Inventory at end of year
Fact.Description: Schedule C line 41. 2026 Schedule C, PDF p. 2: "Inventory at end of year."

Fact.Name: Schedule C line 35
Fact.Description: Inventory at beginning of year, carried to the line 40 total. 2026 Schedule C, PDF p. 2, line 35.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line 36
Fact.Description: Purchases less cost of items withdrawn for personal use. 2026 Schedule C, PDF p. 2, line 36. Rounded half up to the nearest dollar, the same way the other Schedule C lines in this tool are rounded.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line 37
Fact.Description: Cost of labor. 2026 Schedule C, PDF p. 2, line 37.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line 38
Fact.Description: Materials and supplies. 2026 Schedule C, PDF p. 2, line 38.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line 39
Fact.Description: Other costs. 2026 Schedule C, PDF p. 2, line 39.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line 40
Fact.Description: 2026 Schedule C, PDF p. 2, line 40: "Add lines 35 through 39."

Fact.Name: Schedule C line 41
Fact.Description: Inventory at end of year. 2026 Schedule C, PDF p. 2, line 41.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line 42
Fact.Description: 2026 Schedule C, PDF p. 2, line 42: "Cost of goods sold. Subtract line 41 from line 40. Enter the result here and on line 4."

Fact.Name: Part III is filled in while the business says it has no inventory
Fact.Description: True when the filer says there is no inventory, but a Part III method (cost, lower of cost or market, or other) is selected or any Part III amount is greater than zero. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C, PDF p. 16: choosing not to keep an inventory means Part III is not completed. That contradiction stops the return. The section 471(c) no-inventory method with every Part III amount blank or zero is not this contradiction. An unanswered method or amount is not treated as a contradiction.

Fact.Name: Simple Part III cost of goods sold is in scope
Fact.Description: True only when this business has inventory, values it at cost or lower of cost or market, reports no change in quantities, costs, or valuations (line 34 no), the 3-prior-year average does not exceed $32,000,000, the filer is not a tax shelter, and line 35 is not different from last year's closing inventory. Line 42 below zero is a separate stop and is not part of this fact, so the amount screen can still be answered. Anything else leaves line 4 incomplete. 26 U.S.C. 471(c)(1), 263A(i)(1). 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C, PDF p. 16.

Fact.Name: Ask whether line 35 differs from last year's closing inventory
Fact.Description: True when Part III is otherwise the simple path: inventory, line 33a or 33b, line 34 no, the 3-prior-year average does not exceed $32,000,000, and the filer is not a tax shelter. The line 35 screener is asked then. 2026 Schedule C, PDF p. 2, line 35.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line 42 is below zero
Fact.Description: 2026 Schedule C, PDF p. 2, line 42: "Cost of goods sold. Subtract line 41 from line 40. Enter the result here and on line 4." True when that subtraction is below zero. The result is not replaced with zero. On the simple path that stops the return and leaves line 4 incomplete. Complete and false when this business has no inventory path.

Fact.Name: Line 35 differs from last year's closing inventory
Fact.Description: 2026 Schedule C, PDF p. 2, line 35: "Inventory at beginning of year. If different from last year's closing inventory, attach explanation." 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C, PDF p. 17, Line 35: "If there is a difference between last year's closing inventory and the refigured amount, attach an explanation." This tool does not attach that explanation. The screener answer is this fact on the simple path. Yes stops the return. Complete and false when this business has no inventory path.

Fact.Name: Part III cannot be figured
Fact.Description: Stops the return, and leaves line 4 incomplete, when line 33c is Other, line 34 is yes, the 3-prior-year average exceeds $32,000,000, the filer is a tax shelter, line 42 is below zero, line 35 differs from last year's closing inventory, the section 471(c) no-inventory method is claimed while Part III is still required, or the filer says there is no inventory but a Part III method or amount is still present. Cost or lower of cost or market with line 34 no, a 3-prior-year average that does not exceed $32,000,000, the filer not a tax shelter, line 42 at least zero, and line 35 equal to last year's closing inventory is not a stop.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line 33a checkbox
Fact.Description: Checked when closing inventory is valued at cost.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line 33b checkbox
Fact.Description: Checked when closing inventory is valued at the lower of cost or market.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line 33c checkbox
Fact.Description: Checked when line 33c applies. That return is stopped.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line 34 Yes
Fact.Description: Checked when quantities, costs, or valuations changed. That return is stopped.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line 34 No
Fact.Description: Checked when a simple method is used and quantities, costs, and valuations did not change.

Fact.Name: Car, truck, or vehicle-loan expense
Fact.Description: Schedule C line 9 and line 16b. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 2 (line 16b is vehicle loan interest) and PDF p. 7, Line 9. Standard mileage, actual vehicle expenses, and vehicle loan interest need Form 4562 or Part IV. Yes stops the return. Lines 9 and 16b stay blank.

Fact.Name: Depreciation or section 179
Fact.Description: Schedule C line 13. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 8, Line 13. Depreciation and section 179 need Form 4562. Yes stops the return. 26 U.S.C. 167, 179.

Fact.Name: Depletion
Fact.Description: Schedule C line 12. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf) line 12. Depletion (26 U.S.C. 611) stops the return. Line 12 stays blank.

Fact.Name: Rent of vehicles, machinery, or equipment
Fact.Description: Schedule C line 20a. Rent of vehicles, machinery, and equipment can require an inclusion amount and Form 4562 for listed property. Yes stops the return. Line 20a stays blank.

Fact.Name: Business use of home
Fact.Description: Schedule C line 30. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 11, Line 30: Form 8829 or the simplified method. Either method stops the return. Line 30 stays blank, so a supported return's line 31 equals line 29.

Fact.Name: Energy efficient commercial buildings deduction
Fact.Description: Schedule C line 27a. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 11, Line 27a: attach Form 7205. Yes stops the return. Line 27a stays blank. 26 U.S.C. 179D.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line-item questions started
Fact.Description: True when any Part I amount, stop question, or expense question for this business has been answered. A return that only stored the single expense total has not started the line-item path.

Fact.Name: Use the single expense total
Fact.Description: The pre-line-item expense total is used only when it is answered and no line-item question is answered. That keeps returns which stored one total on gross receipts minus that total, and keeps lines 2, 4, and 6 at zero. Once a line-item answer exists, the total is ignored so it is not deducted twice.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line 1
Fact.Description: Gross receipts or sales. 2026 Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1040sc.pdf), line 1. 26 U.S.C. 61. The amount the filer entered, or, on a return that still uses the single expense total, the same derived gross receipts (unanswered treated as zero only on that older path). Unanswered on the line-item path stays incomplete.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line 2
Fact.Description: Returns and allowances. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 7. Zero on the single-total path, where line 2 was blank.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line 3
Fact.Description: 2026 Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1040sc.pdf), line 3: subtract line 2 from line 1.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line 4
Fact.Description: Cost of goods sold. 2026 Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1040sc.pdf), line 4: "Cost of goods sold (from line 42)." Zero on the single-total path, and zero when the filer says there is no inventory and Part III is not filled in. When simple Part III applies, line 42 is at least zero, and line 35 equals last year's closing inventory, line 4 is line 42 (line 40 minus line 41). A negative line 42 is not replaced with zero. A Part III stop leaves line 4 incomplete rather than zero. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C, PDF p. 16.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line 5
Fact.Description: 2026 Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1040sc.pdf), line 5: gross profit, subtract line 4 from line 3.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line 6
Fact.Description: Other income. Zero on the single-total path. The entered amount on the line-item path, including when a stop applies; the stop keeps the net profit off Schedule 1.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line 7
Fact.Description: 2026 Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1040sc.pdf), line 7: gross income, add lines 5 and 6. 26 U.S.C. 61.

Fact.Name: Has deductible business expenses
Fact.Description: Whether this business has ordinary and necessary expenses under 26 U.S.C. 162(a) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/162). No makes every Part II line and line 28 zero. Yes requires at least one line.

Fact.Name: Schedule C expense lines
Fact.Description: Part II and Part V lines the filer has for this business. Each selected line is deducted under 26 U.S.C. 162(a) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/162) except meals, which are limited by 26 U.S.C. 274(n).

Fact.Name: At least one expense line selected
Fact.Description: An empty list while the filer said there are deductible expenses leaves line 28 incomplete. True when any supported line was selected.

Fact.Name: Expense line chosen: advertising

Fact.Name: Schedule C line 24b

Fact.Name: PA-40 line 4 meals add-back (100% PA minus federal 50%)
Fact.Description: PA-40 C (EX) 03-26 instructions: federal/PA differences include "meals, travel, and entertainment expense deduction of 100 percent by Pennsylvania." Federal Schedule C line 24b takes 50 percent under 26 U.S.C. 274(n) when mealsAreStandardHalfLimit. The add-back is writableMeals minus line24bDeductibleMeals. /scheduleCBusinesses/*/paNetProfitOrLoss subtracts it from federal line 31, and PA-40 line 4 (/paLine4) is the sum of those nets, so Pennsylvania deducts the full meal cost (PA-40 C (EX) 03-26 line 31). Zero on the single-expense-total path and when meals were not chosen. Incomplete when a non-50-percent meal limit applies (that case is already /flowKnockoutScheduleCOutOfScope).

Fact.Name: PA Schedule C line 18 interest
Fact.Description: PA-40 C (EX) 03-26 line 18, interest on business indebtedness. Sum of federal Schedule C lines 16a and 16c. Line 16b (vehicle interest) is a stop and is not included. 72 P.S. §7303(a)(2) (https://codes.findlaw.com/pa/title-72-ps-taxation-and-fiscal-affairs/pa-st-sect-72-7303/).

Fact.Name: PA Schedule C line 31 travel and entertainment

Federal line 24a plus federal line 24b plus /paMealsAddBack (the half of meals federal line 24b omits under 26 U.S.C. 274(n)).

Fact.Name: PA Schedule C line 38 total expenses
Fact.Description: PA-40 C (EX) 03-26 line 38, the sum of lines 6 through 37. Federal Schedule C line 28 (/totalExpenses, which includes only the 50 percent federal meal deduction) plus /paMealsAddBack, so the printed total deducts meals at 100 percent. Line 39 is line 5 minus this amount.

Fact.Name: PA Schedule C line 39 net profit or loss

PA-40 line 4 (/paLine4) sums this fact for a full-year resident. 72 P.S. §7303(a)(2). A loss is allowed; the printed amount is the size of the loss and the line 39 oval is filled.

Fact.Name: Schedule C business needs a form this tool does not compute
Fact.Description: True when Part III cannot be figured (line 33c, a line 34 change, a 3-prior-year average over $32,000,000, a tax shelter, line 42 below zero, line 35 different from last year's closing inventory, the section 471(c) no-inventory method claimed together with Part III, or Part III amounts while the filer says there is no inventory), or a vehicle, depreciation, depletion, equipment rent, a home office, the line 27a deduction, a non-50-percent meal, wage credits, interest that must be allocated, new amortization, a fourth Part V line, or line 6 income that belongs on another form applies. A yes on any stop is enough; later blanks do not turn it off. Cost or lower of cost or market, line 34 no, a 3-prior-year average that does not exceed $32,000,000, the filer not a tax shelter, line 42 at least zero, and line 35 equal to last year's closing inventory is not a stop.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line 31 is a loss
Fact.Description: 2026 Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1040sc.pdf), line 32: complete line 32 only when there is a loss. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 16: you do not complete line 32 if line 7 is more than the total of lines 28 and 30. A profit is not an at-risk or passive stop.

Fact.Name: All investment is at risk
Fact.Description: Schedule C line 32a. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 16, Line 32. 26 U.S.C. 465 (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/465). All at risk, together with material participation, lets the loss flow. Line 32b (some investment is not at risk) needs Form 6198 and stops the return.

Fact.Name: Schedule C loss needs Form 6198 or Form 8582
Fact.Description: A loss without material participation needs Form 8582. 26 U.S.C. 469 (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/469). A loss that is not fully at risk needs Form 6198. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 16, Lines 31 and 32. A profit does not use this stop. The loss amount itself is still computed; this fact only stops filing, so the limit does not depend on the net in a circle.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line 32a
Fact.Description: Checked only for a loss when all investment is at risk.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line 32b
Fact.Description: Checked only for a loss when some investment is not at risk. That return is stopped.

Fact.Name: This Schedule C business is out of scope
Fact.Description: False when the line-item questions were not started, so a single expense total is not an out-of-scope business. True when they were started and a form stop or a loss-limit stop applies.

Fact.Name: Schedule C businesses that are out of scope
Fact.Description: Businesses whose line-item answers need a form or a loss limit this tool does not compute.

Fact.Name: Knockout: Schedule C line needs a form or loss limit not computed here
Fact.Description: Stops filing and printing when a Schedule C business, after the line-item questions are started, has Part III that this tool does not figure (line 33c Other, line 34 yes, a 3-prior-year average annual gross receipts amount greater than $32,000,000 under Rev. Proc. 2025-32 §4.30 and 26 U.S.C. 448(c), a tax shelter under 26 U.S.C. 448(d)(3), line 42 below zero, line 35 different from last year's closing inventory, the section 471(c) no-inventory method claimed while Part III is still required, or Part III filled in after a no to inventory), car or truck expenses or vehicle-loan interest (lines 9 and 16b, Form 4562), depreciation or section 179 (line 13, Form 4562), depletion (line 12), rent of vehicles or equipment (line 20a), business use of the home (line 30, Form 8829 or the simplified method), the energy efficient commercial buildings deduction (line 27a, Form 7205), meals that are not limited to 50 percent (line 24b, 26 U.S.C. 274(n)), wages reduced by an employment credit (line 26), interest that must be allocated (lines 16a and 16c), amortization that begins this year (Form 4562-B), a fourth Part V line, line 6 income that belongs on Form 4136, 6478, or 4797, a loss without material participation (Form 8582, 26 U.S.C. 469), or a loss that is not fully at risk (line 32b, Form 6198, 26 U.S.C. 465). Complete and false when self-employment income was not asked, was answered no, there are no businesses, or the business only has the single expense total. An unanswered line-item question on a business that was started stays incomplete, so that return is not treated as in scope.

Fact.Name: Total Schedule C net profit or (loss)
Fact.Description: Sum of Schedule C net profit/(loss) for Schedule 1 line 3 → Form 1040 line 8 (via Schedule 1 line 10). Cite: Schedule C instructions; Form 1040 Schedule 1 line 3.

Fact.Name: Schedule C net profit included in earned income
Fact.Description: Earned income from self-employment for the EITC, CDCC and ACTC = Schedule C net profit (Schedule SE line 3) minus the deductible part of SE tax (Schedule 1 line 15, Schedule SE line 13), 26 U.S.C. 32(c)(2)(A)(ii) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/32#c_2_A): "net earnings from self-employment ... determined with regard to the deduction allowed to the taxpayer by section 164(f)". Instructions for Form 1040 (2025), PDF p. 47, EIC Worksheet B, Part 1: "1a. Enter the amount from Schedule SE, Part I, line 3. ... d. Enter the amount from Schedule SE, Part I, line 13. ... e. Subtract line 1d from line 1c." Under $400 of net earnings no SE tax applies, so this is the Schedule C line 31 net profit (Worksheet B Part 2, line 2b). 2026 draft Instructions for Form 2441, PDF p. 5, lines 4 and 5: "2. The amount shown on Schedule SE (Form 1040), line 3, minus any deduction you claim on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 15." #117: floored at $0 because a loss is not modeled; a loss stops the return wherever it would change a credit (/flowKnockoutScheduleCEarnedIncomeCredits).
